rawFindings.title: Removed check for IP addresses in req.subdomains getter
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used `isIP` to detect if the host is an IP address, in which case it returned the entire IP as the only subdomain segment. This behavior prevents splitting IP addresses on dots, which makes sense since IP addresses are not domain names. The new code unconditionally splits the host string by '.' and reverses the array without checking if it is an IP address. This will erroneously split IP addresses such as '127.0.0.1' into ['1','0','0','127'], which is incorrect for subdomains r
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the original IP detection logic using `isIP` and conditionally return the IP as the sole subdomain element if host is an IP address. For example:

var isIP = require('net').isIP;

rawFindings.title: Removed tests for req.subdomains IP address handling
rawFindings.explanation: The tests verifying that req.subdomains correctly handle IP addresses (return empty array when IP is host, or array with full IP when subdomain offset is 0) were completely removed. These tests ensured that the behavior around IP hosts was correct and prevent regressions. Removing these tests reduces coverage and allows the regression introduced in lib/request.js to go unnoticed.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the removed tests or add new tests to cover the IP address handling in req.subdomains getter to ensure correct handling of IP address hosts and prevent regressions.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect subdomains parsing for IP addresses in req.subdomains getter
rawFindings.explanation: The removed code used to check if the host is an IP address (using isIP). If it was an IP, it returned the host as a single-item array; otherwise, it split the hostname by '.' and reversed the parts. The new code always splits the host by '.' and reverses it regardless. IP addresses like '127.0.0.1' or '[::1]' contain dots or colons, and splitting them by '.' produces arrays like ['1', '0', '0', '127'] which is incorrect for IP addresses. rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the IP check using require('net').isIP and if the host is an IP, return it whole in an array instead of splitting into subdomain parts. This prevents IP addresses from being treated as hostnames and improperly split into subdomains.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of IP addresses in req.subdomains property
rawFindings.explanation: The original implementation used net.isIP(host) to detect if the host is an IP address, in which case it returned [host] as the array of subdomains. This was removed, so now the code always splits the host string on '.' and reverses the resulting array. For an IP address like '127.0.0.1', this results in ['1','0','0','127'] instead of ['127.0.0.1'], which breaks the expected behavior of req.subdomains when host is an IP address.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the IP address detection using net.isIP(host). Return [host] as the subdomains array if host is an IP address, else split by '.' and reverse as before. Alternatively, add explicit handling to detect IP addresses to return the whole host as a single-element array.
